application.name: Super Productivity
application.description: An advanced personal task manager: task lists with drag reorder, integrated time tracking and timeboxing, projects, worklog and daily summary, metrics, pomodoro, reminders, notes and bookmarks, schema-driven settings, and full import/export
application.backend: none for the core flow — all state is local, persisted through localforage and browser local storage in src/app/core/persistence. Optional Jira, Google Drive/Sheets and GitHub integrations exist but are off by default.
application.desktopSidecar: An Electron 6 shell lives in electron/ and is the manifest's `main` entry point. It is out of scope for the web fixture and was never invoked.

source.ownerRenameNote: The upstream owner moved from a personal account to an organisation between the scout pass and this ingest. GitHub answers the old path with a 301 to the same numeric repository id. The redirect was recorded and not followed; the canonical path was probed explicitly. The pinned commit, tree and licence blob are content-addressed and unchanged by the rename.

gitLargeFileStorage.note: The scout claimed no LFS. Every blob was byte-scanned for the LFS pointer preamble anyway, on the factoriolab lane's lesson. The tree is self-contained.

toolchain.compiler: pre-Ivy ViewEngine, AOT — enableIvy appears in zero of the 967 blobs and Angular 8.2 defaults to ViewEngine
toolchain.differentialLoading: partial — a polyfills-es5 chunk is emitted alongside the modern polyfills chunk, but a single es5 main bundle, because tsconfig sets target es5 rather than es2015
toolchain.state: @ngrx/store 8.5.2 with effects, entity, data and store-devtools
toolchain.styling: SCSS through node-sass 4, themed by angular-material-css-vars 0.1.6 over CSS custom properties
toolchain.persistence: localforage 1.7 with lz-string compression in a web worker
toolchain.webWorkers: tsconfig.worker.json wired through the builder's webWorkerTsConfig option; two application workers (lz, reminder) compile and emit

dependencyClosure.lockState: pinned-upstream — a complete yarn.lock is committed and `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` succeeded against it unmodified
dependencyClosure.declaredDrift: Two devDependencies are declared as the floating dist-tag "latest": angular-material-css-vars (lock-pinned 0.1.6) and angular2-promise-buttons (lock-pinned 4.0.1). The lockfile is the only thing holding them at their 2019 versions.

localPathDependency.note: an in-tree schematics helper; no external acquisition surface

legacyCell.platform: darwin-x64 executed on darwin-arm64 through Rosetta 2
legacyCell.source: .travis.yml pins `node_js: '12'`. The patch level and the yarn version are this ingest's choices, both era-consistent with the 2019-12 tag.
legacyCell.label: repository-declared as to Node major, era-consistent as to patch and as to yarn

productionBuildAsAcquired.scope: web application only; the Electron sidecar was never invoked

baseline.significance: The first Angular cohort fixture in this corpus to install frozen and build production green on the first attempt with zero deviations.

knownHazardsForLaterUnits: src/index.html hard-codes a Google Fonts stylesheet link, and ngsw-config.json prefetches fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com. Serving this fixture unmodified issues third-party requests on every page load with no user action. Any browser-witness unit must block or stub those two hosts.

The production build emits a real ngsw service worker (ngsw-worker.js, ngsw.json, safety-worker.js). It is recorded, not disabled — a service-worker-free variant must be a labeled deviation, never the unlabeled baseline.

package.json `main` is ./electron/main.js and `yarn start` launches Electron, not a web server. The web dev server is `yarn startFrontend`. Do not assume the default scripts serve a browser application.

The `buildFrontend` script prefixes the build with `yarn preCheck`, which runs lint and the full unit-test suite. The baseline deliberately invoked the bare ng build instead; anyone using the repository script gets a test run too.

jira2md resolves over git protocol from a repository this project does not control, with no registry fallback and no lockfile integrity hash. If that commit ever becomes unfetchable, the closure cannot be reconstructed from the lockfile alone.
Two devDependencies declare the floating tag "latest". Regenerating or upgrading the lockfile silently loses both 2019 pins.

The Jira, Google Drive/Sheets and GitHub integrations are off by default but reachable from the settings surface; enabling one during a witness run would open egress to the hosts recorded in admission.json.
nonclaims: This manifest records an acquired identity, a licence position, a dependency closure and one baseline install and production build. It establishes no browser behavior, runtime correctness, migration feasibility, pilot status, production readiness, certification, or legal approval.
A green production build means the bundle compiles and emits. No browser was opened by the ingesting unit, so nothing here shows the application boots or renders.
